key_insight: The paper presents a reliable evaluation framework for instruction-following in multimodal large language models that centers on visual instructions, showing that text-focused benchmarks miss important visual constraints and proposing targeted tests and metrics to close that gap.
problem_solved: Existing instruction-following benchmarks focus primarily on verbal/textual instructions and therefore fail to capture implicit, image-specific constraints (e.g., referential, spatial, occlusion-related requirements), producing incomplete or misleading assessments of MLLMs' adherence to user intent in visual contexts.
method: Create a visual-centric instruction-following benchmark that covers explicit and implicit instruction types across diverse image scenarios (referential, spatial, occlusion, multi-step reasoning).

Define a combined evaluation protocol using targeted test suites and fidelity metrics, integrating automated scoring and focused human evaluation to measure adherence to user-specified visual constraints.
Analyze model behaviors to identify common failure modes and provide guidelines for improving training and evaluation practices for visual instruction following.
impact: Provides practitioners with targeted tools and metrics to more accurately evaluate and improve multimodal models' alignment with user intent in vision-language tasks, enabling safer, more reliable deployment in real-world visual applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image + user instruction -> MLLM -> fidelity metrics (automated + human) showing evaluation flow
Task cards: side-by-side examples of instruction types (explicit vs implicit) with correct and incorrect model responses
Bar/heatmap chart: comparative model performance across instruction categories to highlight strengths and weaknesses
Annotated failure-case images showing missed constraints (e.g., wrong referent, ignored occlusion) with brief explanations
paper_title: Empowering Reliable Visual-Centric Instruction Following in MLLMs
paper_authors: Weilei He, Feng Ju, Zhiyuan Fan, Rui Min, Minhao Cheng
